reasoning: Both stories are valid, safe to open in edit mode, and handle a live title and two-way selection correctly. Attempt A meets the user's explicit request to try a really long title with a `LongTitle` toggle. Attempt B gives no easy way to do that. A's only defect is a StyLua line-wrap failure, which is trivial to fix. B's misses are about what the user asked for: no long-title preset, plus a stray print. I pick A, by a narrow margin.

criteria.note: BlockPicker.story.luau returns `{ vide = Vide, controls = controls, story = ... }` with Vide from ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Vide, and `story` returns the picker.

criteria.criterion: Controls built from BlockTypes.List, with a text title and an easy long title
criteria.note: `UILabs.Choose(blockNames)` is built from `BlockTypes.List`, `Title = "Blocks"` is a text control, and the `LongTitle` boolean swaps in `LONG_TITLE` with one click.

The `Title` prop is widened to `string | () -> string`, and the story passes a derived function that reads `controlValues.Title()` or `LongTitle()`, so the label updates live; the game caller's plain string still type-checks.

criteria.criterion: Selection driven by both the control and tile clicks
criteria.note: A local `source` is passed as both `Selected` and `Select`, and an `effect` copies the `Selected` control into it, so both the control and a tile click move the highlight.
It requires only BlockTypes, UILabs, Vide, and BlockPicker, never yields, and creates nothing outside the returned picker.
